# Git Panel Scope

## How To Build

A GitPanelScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A GitPanelScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Title

null

## Counted

false

## Height

fit

## Scrolls

false

## Panel

It has no header: its contents start at its top edge, on the theme's base surface.
It shows no count of what it lists.
It is only as tall as its contents need, taking no more of its sidebar's height.
Its contents never scroll: it is as tall as they are.

## Concept

### Pitch

A very basic git panel for the repository the ProjectDirectoryScope is in, as the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope) knows it: see what has changed at a glance, write a commit message, commit, push, and pull.

### Shape

#### Description

A compact panel. It is shown only while the project is inside a git repository.

#### Look

The panel's top row, the branch, is its header: 32 pixels tall, on the ribbon's tab row colour, #333333 in dark mode. Beneath it, the panel's body is on the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode, with 8 pixels of padding at either side and at the bottom, and 4 pixels between one thing and the next. There is no line between the header and the body, nor between the file tree and the header: the change of colour is the edge. Every box and button in it is square, with no rounded corners and no border, and the Pull and Push buttons are square too.

#### Branch

The top row shows a branch icon, then the branch from the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope), or "Detached HEAD", in regular text, beside how many commits it is ahead of its upstream (↑) and behind it (↓), muted, each only when not zero. At the right end are a Pull button, a cloud-download icon, and a Push button, a cloud-upload icon, ghost icon buttons with tooltips.

#### Summary

Below the branch, a line counts the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope)'s changes, leaving out any kind with none, as "2 modified · 1 untracked", or "No changes". At the right end of that line, how many lines were added (+, in green) and removed (−, in red). The count is in small, muted text. The files themselves are not listed, since the [FileTreeScope](../file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope) shows them. The summary refreshes as the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope) does, and straight after anything the panel does.

#### Commit Notes

Above the message box, a box for each commit note, in the order they were added, on the ribbon's tab row colour, holding the note in small text that wraps onto as many lines as it needs, growing to fit it, and can be edited; <Enter> in a note starts a new line within it. A small button to remove it shows at its top right while it is hovered. Each task that adds a note, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says, adds a one-line summary of what it changed, once the harness has written it, quickly, in the same way as a written

##### Message

from what the task asked and the harness's own summary of what

it did, at most 72 characters in the imperative mood, as commit-note.pi, of the [BakedSystemPromptsScope](../../../scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope), asks. Notes are saved with the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../../scope/project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, as they are added, edited, and removed, so they survive a restart, and are never themselves committed.

#### Message

A commit message box, a [GrowingTextInputScope](../growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input-scope) growing to 10 rows at most, so it starts at a single row. On the tree's darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, in the editor's monospace font, it reads "Commit Message…" while empty.

#### Writing AMessage

A "Generate" button, with a sparkles icon, on the ribbon's tab row colour, at the left of the row beneath the message box, has the harness write the commit message from what has changed, and puts it in the message box, replacing what was there. It is quick: a small, fast model, at low effort, with no tools, handed only the list of changed files and as much of the diff as fits in a small, fixed amount. The message is a summary line of at most 72 characters in the imperative mood, followed, only if it helps, by a few short bullet points, as commit-message.pi, of the [BakedSystemPromptsScope](../../../scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope), asks. The button is disabled while there are no changes.

#### Committing

A primary "Commit" button, at the right end of that row, on the ribbon's button colour, #444444 in dark mode, with no icon, commits every change, new files included. The commit message is what was typed, then a blank line, then each note that isn't blank as a line of its own starting "- "; with nothing typed, it is the notes alone. Once committed, the message box and the notes are cleared. It is disabled while there is neither a message nor a note, or there are no changes.

#### Pushing And Pulling

Push pushes the branch, setting its upstream on origin first if it has none.
Pull fetches the branch's upstream. With nothing new it says the branch is already up to date. When only the upstream has moved on, the branch fast-forwards to it. When both have moved on, the upstream is merged in automatically, as long as the merge has no conflicts. If it would conflict, the pull is cancelled before anything changes: the branch, its files, and the index stay exactly as they were, no merge is left in progress, and an error names the files that would have conflicted. Pull is disabled while the branch has no upstream.

#### Feedback

While the panel is committing, pushing, pulling, or writing a message, that button shows a spinner and the others are disabled. Committing, pushing, and pulling say so in a notification when they succeed; a pull says whether it was already up to date, pulled, or pulled and merged. Anything that fails says why in an error notification.

## How To Build

A ProjectSidebarScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A ProjectSidebarScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

- [FileTreeScope](../file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope)
- [GitPanelScope](../git-panel/index.md#git-panel-scope)

## Sidebar

It runs along the left of what it sits beside, with a thin line down its right edge, where the two meet. It is resized by dragging that edge: it starts 260 pixels wide and can't be dragged narrower than 160.
It holds its panels one above the other, in the order it lists them, each across its full width. A single thin line, in the theme's line colour, lies between one panel and the next, never two, unless the next panel says its own change of colour is the edge. A panel that isn't shown for the moment takes no room and leaves no line.
It is on the theme's base surface, as its panels' bodies are.

## Concept

### Pitch

The [SidebarScope](../sidebar/index.md#sidebar-scope) along the left of the main window's body, holding the tools for finding your way around the project.

### Shape

#### Description

Runs the full height of the body, beneath the ribbon, to the left of everything else in it. The file tree fills it from the top, and the git panel sits along the bottom, underneath it, taking only the height it needs.

#### Others

It is the body's only sidebar on the left. While a task runs, a second one, the running task's referenced spec, slides out at the right of the message list, as the [MessageList](../../../scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list) says.
